title: React UI: Project Completion Meter
businessContext: A project dashboard receives progress values from multiple importers, including values outside the display range.
problemStatement: Export App({ value = 0 }). Accept only finite JavaScript numbers; all other values display zero. Clamp the number to 0–100, then round to the nearest integer. Render an element with role=progressbar, aria-label="Project completion", aria-valuemin="0", aria-valuemax="100", and aria-valuenow equal to the display integer. Show the same integer followed by % in [data-testid="percentage"]. The displayed value must be derived from props rather than copied into mount-only state.
constraints: Numeric strings are invalid and must not be coerced.
The visual fill and accessible numeric value must agree. No animation is required.

testCases.name: Progress above one hundred is clamped
The range and accessible label are explicit

hints: Check typeof and Number.isFinite before applying Math.min and Math.max.
Use one normalized value for the fill, text, and ARIA attributes.
commonMistakes: Coercing numeric strings even though the input contract forbids them.
Updating the text but leaving an inconsistent aria-valuenow.
candidateTasks: Implement the default-exported App component and the documented DOM contract.
Run every interaction journey, explain edge cases, then compare your implementation with the reference.
alternativeApproaches: Extract a small pure helper for derived values; keep input state in the component. Extend with a custom hook only when behavior is reused.
